scope: engine-only pre-event observer correction; no ordinary definitions or admissions

cards.name: Ketramose, the New Dawn
cards.oracle_text:
Menace, lifelink, indestructible
Ketramose can't attack or block unless there are seven or more cards in exile.
Whenever one or more cards are put into exile from graveyards and/or the battlefield during your turn, you draw a card and lose 1 life.

cards.name: Kaya, Spirits' Justice
cards.oracle_text:
Whenever one or more creatures you control and/or creature cards in your graveyard are put into exile, you may choose a creature card from among them. Until end of turn, target token you control becomes a copy of it, except it has flying.
+2: Surveil 2, then exile a card from a graveyard.
+1: Create a 1/1 white and black Spirit creature token with flying.
−2: Exile target creature you control. For each other player, exile up to one target creature that player controls.

primary_rules.contract: Both battlefield and graveyard departures use ability existence and controller immediately before the event.

discrepancy: The previous engine combined pre-event battlefield observers with post-event graveyard observers. Ketramose marks its batch ability as leaves-the-battlefield; Kaya does not explicitly set that flag in its main Java class. The shared Rust event rule follows CR603.10a for both conditions rather than copying post-event eligibility.
implementation: Use the already-frozen shared pre-event ObjectView population for both exile event conditions.
Do not create triggers for simultaneous incoming observers or ability restoration; preserve departing/newly blanked observers and their old controller.
Preserve physical-card/global versus own-creature filtering and exact successful exile links.
No new state, wire fields, or hot allocations; remove post-event population merging.
tests: tests/dft_exile_lookback.rs: seven independent scenarios, both seats and event qualifiers, departing/new/blanked/restored/stolen sources, physical noncreature contrast, owned raw/index/restore through foreign Aura choice
review: Defect independently identified by audit_black_red; complete fix requires two nonauthor scoped reviews at final engine head.
